prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (func_metadata.py): it calls `json.loads()` on any string argument whose annotation is not exactly `str`, so a plain string value passed for a `str | None`-style union parameter that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "{...}") gets silently corrupted into a non-string. Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the union's members instead of the blanket `annotation is not str` check, editing the identical line in `pre_parse_json`. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (func_metadata.py): it calls `json.loads()` on any string argument whose annotation is not exactly `str`, so a plain string value passed for a `str | None`-style union parameter that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "{...}") gets silently corrupted into a non-string. Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the union's members instead of the blanket `annotation is not str` check, editing the identical line in `pre_parse_json`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` and applies it to each union member before checking, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic MCP tool pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None`. PR #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` against the raw union args without unwrapping `Annotated`, so for that same `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` pattern the Annotated-wrapped member is never in `_SIMPLE_TYPES`, `any(...)` is True, and the function still returns True — meaning #2032 does not actually prevent the corruption bug for parameters written with `Annotated`+`Field`, which is the common style in this codebase's own tool signatures. #2032 does cover a broader set of plain (non-Annotated) simple-type unions like `str | int | bool`, but #3056's handling of the Annotated case addresses the more common real-world parameter shape.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` and applies it to each union member before checking, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic MCP tool pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None`. PR #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` against the raw union args without unwrapping `Annotated`, so for that same `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` pattern the Annotated-wrapped member is never in `_SIMPLE_TYPES`, `any(...)` is True, and the function still returns True — meaning #2032 does not actually prevent the corruption bug for parameters written with `Annotated`+`Field`, which is the common style in this codebase's own tool signatures. #2032 does cover a broader set of plain (non-Annotated) simple-type unions like `str | int | bool`, but #3056's handling of the Annotated case addresses the more common real-world parameter shape.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962's fix and its added regression test explicitly cite SEP-1577's spec text — tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by tool_use, but there is no requirement that tool_use MUST be followed by a tool_result — giving a documented protocol basis for not raising. #3053 takes the opposite position (raising a new, more specific ValueError in the same no-tool_result case) without addressing that spec language, so it reintroduces the exact behavior #2962's regression test asserts should not happen.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the exact same conditional block in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) to handle the case where a previous-message tool_use has no corresponding tool_result in the current message (both cite issue #2960), but they implement opposite, mutually exclusive fixes: #2962 adds a `has_tool_results` guard so the ID-matching check (and thus any error) is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, deliberately allowing tool_use to go unanswered; #3053 instead adds an explicit `raise ValueError` when `not has_tool_results`, keeping/clarifying an error in that same scenario. Merging both is impossible without one immediately overriding/contradicting the other. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs replace the same naive substring-based WWW-Authenticate parsing with a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer. #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params additionally scopes extraction to the specific Bearer challenge by detecting scheme tokens, correctly handling headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...'), whereas #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only splits params after the first space and assumes a single challenge, which would misparse multi-challenge headers.
